project: issue-126 Standalone Agent Jobs: first-class agent execution independent of workflow
description: Open the Runner coordination layer with an additive WorkDispatch owner-kind dimension (workflow | agent-job) so that a standalone AgentJobGrain can own its lifecycle (pending → running → completed/failed), dispatch directly via RunnerRegistry (bypassing WorkflowBacklogGrain), receive ReportResult, and be exercised end-to-end through a minimal validation HTTP API. The workflow coordination path must remain byte-equivalent for owner-kind = workflow.

tasks.title: Open Runner coordination layer for WorkDispatch owner-kind (workflow arm unchanged)
tasks.spec: specs/agent-job/spec.md#Requirement: WorkDispatch carries owner-kind dimension; specs/agent-job/spec.md#Requirement: Runner accepts work from either owner identity; specs/agent-job/spec.md#Requirement: IsWorkRunnableAsync routes by owner-kind; specs/agent-job/spec.md#Requirement: ReportResultAsync routes by owner-kind; specs/agent-job/spec.md#Requirement: Workflow coordination path behavior is preserved
tasks.description: Extend the C# WorkDispatch record with an OwnerKind field ("workflow" | "agent-job", default "workflow") and an optional AgentJobId field using new [Id(n)] serializer slots so the existing workflow wire format remains decodable. Introduce the IAgentJobGrain interface as the routing contract (GetIsWorkRunnableAsync / ReportResultAsync / GetCurrentWorkIdAsync-equivalent surface) — interface only, no implementation in this task. In RunnerGrain, extract the existing workflow body of AssignWorkAsync validation, IsWorkRunnableAsync, and ReportResultAsync verbatim into private helpers and add a switch on work.OwnerKind at each of the three weld points; the workflow arm calls the verbatim helper, the agent-job arm calls IAgentJobGrain. The agent-job arm shares the existing _works map and ActiveWorkflowCount slot accounting. Workflow behavior must stay byte-identical.
acceptanceCriteria: IRunnerGrain.cs WorkDispatch record has OwnerKind (default "workflow") and AgentJobId (default null) fields with fresh [Id(n)] slots; existing field ids and order are unchanged

IAgentJobGrain.cs is added under packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Agent/Jobs/ declaring the routing-surface methods that RunnerGrain's agent-job arm calls (at minimum: a runnable/cancellation check, ReportResultAsync(runnerId, workId, result), and a current-work query if needed)

RunnerGrain.AssignWorkAsync accepts a dispatch with owner-kind=agent-job and a non-empty AgentJobId (no WorkflowRunId) and returns Assigned; rejects when the owner identity for the declared kind or WorkId is missing (invalid-work)

RunnerGrain.IsWorkRunnableAsync branches by OwnerKind: workflow arm calls IWorkflowGrain (GetClaimedRunnerIdAsync + GetRunStatusAsync + GetCurrentWorkIdAsync) with the exact pre-change rule; agent-job arm calls IAgentJobGrain

RunnerGrain.ReportResultAsync branches by OwnerKind: workflow arm calls IWorkflowGrain.ReportResultAsync + GetRunStatusAsync and returns a byte-equivalent RunnerWorkReportResult; agent-job arm calls IAgentJobGrain.ReportResultAsync and never touches IWorkflowGrain
Agent-job work shares the existing _works map and MaxWorkflowSlots / ActiveWorkflowCount slot accounting

Unit tests cover the agent-job arm of all three weld points using a fake IAgentJobGrain (accepted dispatch without WorkflowRunId, runnable routes to the job grain, result routes to the job grain, missing-owner rejected)
Unit tests assert the workflow arm is unchanged for the same inputs (claim check, status check, current-work-id check; report result + run status readback)
Workflow regression suite (workflow-run, workflow-engine, ralph-task-execution specs) passes without modification
A serialization round-trip test decodes a pre-change WorkDispatch payload (no OwnerKind/AgentJobId fields) into the new record and verifies OwnerKind defaults to "workflow" and AgentJobId to null
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Runner/Grains/IRunnerGrain.cs (extended WorkDispatch), packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Agent/Jobs/IAgentJobGrain.cs (new interface), packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Runner/Grains/RunnerGrain.cs (owner-kind branching at the three weld points); new owner-kind routing + serialization tests under packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests
tasks.notes: Design Decisions 1, 2, 4, 7. The workflow arm must be extracted verbatim into private helpers (IsWorkRunnableForWorkflowAsync / ReportResultForWorkflowAsync / AssignWorkValidationForWorkflowAsync) so the agent-job arm is the only new code path and regression risk is bounded. IAgentJobGrain is introduced here only as the routing contract; its implementation is T-002. Runner TS types are intentionally NOT changed (Decision 7): the server is the only owner-aware boundary.

tasks.title: Implement AgentJobGrain lifecycle, result ownership, direct RunnerRegistry dispatch, and silo wiring
tasks.spec: specs/agent-job/spec.md#Requirement: AgentJobGrain owns lifecycle and result; specs/agent-job/spec.md#Requirement: Agent jobs dispatch directly via RunnerRegistry
tasks.description: Implement AgentJobGrain satisfying the IAgentJobGrain interface from T-001 and wire it into the Orleans silo as part of the same deliverable slice. The grain owns an in-memory pending → running → completed/failed lifecycle (no [PersistentState], not [Reentrant]). On activation/submit it queries IRunnerRegistryGrain.ListEligibleRunnersAsync(projectId), selects an online runner with a free slot (via IRunnerGrain.GetRuntimeStateAsync), and calls runner.AssignWorkAsync with a WorkDispatch whose OwnerKind=agent-job and AgentJobId is set, transitioning the job pending → running on acceptance. When no slot is available it retries on an exponential backoff (1s → 60s cap) up to a total bound (default 10 min), then fails with runner-unavailable. It accepts the runner's ReportResultAsync as the authoritative terminal result, rejects reports against terminal jobs, and applies a grain-level job timeout (default 10 min) that fails the job if no report arrives. WorkflowBacklogGrain is never called. The grain must be registered in the Orleans silo so GrainFactory.GetGrain<IAgentJobGrain>(key) resolves an active activation, its constructor dependencies resolve from DI, and backoff/timeout defaults come from a single configuration knob.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Agent/Jobs/AgentJobGrain.cs implements IAgentJobGrain with in-memory state and is neither [Reentrant] nor [PersistentState]
Submitting/activating a job transitions it pending → running when a runner accepts AssignWorkAsync, recording the runner id
A successful WorkResult via ReportResultAsync transitions the job to completed and stores status, message, output, and artifacts as the owned terminal result
A failed WorkResult transitions the job to failed and stores the failure evidence as the owned terminal result
ReportResultAsync against an already completed/failed job is rejected and the prior terminal result is preserved

Dispatch queries IRunnerRegistryGrain.ListEligibleRunnersAsync and calls IRunnerGrain.AssignWorkAsync directly with OwnerKind=agent-job and AgentJobId set; the dispatch WorkDispatch carries prompt/model/workspace via uses/with/variables as the generic execution layer expects

When zero runners have a free slot, the job stays pending and retries on an exponential backoff (1s → 60s cap) until a configured total bound; reaching the bound transitions the job to failed with a runner-unavailable reason
AgentJobGrain never calls any IWorkflowBacklogGrain method (asserted in tests)
A grain-level job timeout (default 10 min, configurable) transitions a running job to failed with a report-timeout reason if no result arrives

AgentJobGrain is registered in the Orleans silo configuration so GrainFactory.GetGrain<IAgentJobGrain>(key) resolves an active activation, and its constructor dependencies (IRunnerRegistryGrain via GrainFactory, ILogger<AgentJobGrain>, config for backoff/timeout bounds) resolve from the silo DI container

Backoff and job-timeout defaults are sourced from a single configuration knob (documented defaults: backoff 1s→60s cap, total bound 10 min, job timeout 10 min) so they can be tuned without code change
Existing silo startup and workflow grain registrations are unchanged (no workflow regression)

Unit tests cover: pending→running on dispatch, running→completed on success, running→failed on failure, terminal rejection of further reports, backoff retry when no slot is available, bound-exceeded failure, backlog bypass, job-timeout failure, and grain resolution from the silo
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Agent/Jobs/AgentJobGrain.cs (new), Orleans silo + DI registration for AgentJobGrain, configuration knob for backoff/timeout bounds; AgentJobGrain lifecycle + dispatch + timeout + wiring tests under packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests
tasks.notes: Design Decisions 3, 4, 5 plus the backoff/timeout mitigations from the Risks section. Silo wiring + DI registration + the config knob are included here (not split out) because a grain implementation is not a deliverable functional slice until it is reachable from the silo and its operational bounds are configurable. Slot accounting is shared with workflow runs via MaxWorkflowSlots (Decision 4) — no separate budget. State is in-memory only; loss on silo restart is an accepted v1 trade-off (Decision 5). Keep the grain non-reentrant so the backoff timer and ReportResult cannot race on the lifecycle fields.

tasks.title: Add minimal end-to-end validation HTTP API for agent jobs
tasks.spec: specs/agent-job/spec.md#Requirement: Minimal end-to-end validation API; specs/agent-job/spec.md#Requirement: WorkspaceManager accepts standalone agent-job work
tasks.description: Add packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Agent/Jobs/AgentJobController.cs exposing a single POST endpoint that accepts { prompt, model, workspace }, creates an AgentJobGrain with a generated key, populates the dispatch variables with workspace.path (so WorkspaceManager.ensure takes its existing short-circuit branch) and the prompt/model, awaits the job's terminal result, and returns { status, message, output, artifacts }. The request is bounded by a timeout that produces a structured failed result rather than an opaque 500. Missing required fields are rejected before job creation. The endpoint is validation-only: no auth, no polling, no read-model.
acceptanceCriteria: POST to the new endpoint with { prompt, model, workspace } creates an AgentJobGrain, dispatches it through the engine, awaits terminal state, and returns the job's status/message/output/artifacts

The dispatch variables carry workspace.path so the runner's WorkspaceManager.ensure uses the existing early-return branch (workspace.ts:32-36) — no workspace.ts code change is required (Design Decision 8)
A job that reaches failed returns a structured failure response (status, message, reason) distinguishing job failure from request-handling error
A request missing the prompt field is rejected with a clear validation error and no AgentJobGrain is created
A request that exceeds the await timeout returns a structured timeout result instead of an opaque 500
No changes to packages/runner/src/runtime/workspace.ts are required for the agent-job path (verified by an end-to-end test that supplies only workspace.path)

End-to-end test exercises the full path: HTTP POST → AgentJobGrain → RunnerRegistry dispatch → runner AssignWorkAsync (owner-kind=agent-job) → generic execution layer → ReportResultAsync → IAgentJobGrain → HTTP response
Existing HTTP API surface (http-api spec) is unchanged
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Agent/Jobs/AgentJobController.cs (new endpoint) and route registration; end-to-end validation API tests under packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests
tasks.notes: Design Decision 6 (blocking validation API). Decision 8 means workspace.ts intentionally stays unchanged — the endpoint must always populate variables.workspace.path so the existing short-circuit branch is taken. Authority/auth is an explicit non-goal; add a code comment noting the endpoint is validation-only and must not be exposed on a production edge as-is.
